name: Suriname

findings.financier: Export-Import Bank of China (preferential buyer's credit, about USD 98.5m)
findings.summary: Huawei built Telesur's National Broadband Network, replacing copper with fibre-to-the-curb and fibre-to-the-home, under a USD 115.8m contract financed about 85% by a China Exim loan; completed December 2019, loan later in arrears.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese development finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Huawei is the equipment vendor, so pole prc. Tier 5 on reported completion. USD 115.8m is the contract value as reported by AidData, not a filing. Loan distress (Exim drew on reserve account Feb 2022; arrears reported 2023) is financial, not a reversal. Completed just before 2020 and not reconfirmed as current. Single opened S2 source, so low.

findings.financier: Bank of China, Shenzhen Branch (USD 25m buyer's credit, Sinosure-insured)
findings.summary: A USD 25m Bank of China buyer's credit financed 85% of two Huawei supply-and-install contracts for Telesur's 3G and 4G wireless rollout, implemented 2014 to 2016; the loan was reportedly repaid in full.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese development finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Huawei as RAN/equipment vendor, so pole prc. Tier 5 on reported completion. Contract value not stated (loan covered 85%), so announced value null. Pre-2020 and not reconfirmed; Telesur's 5G (live in Paramaribo since Dec 2019 per Developing Telecoms) had no vendor named, so whether Huawei still supplies the mobile network is unconfirmed.

findings.local_actor: National Security Directorate (DNVS), Command Center; Ministry of Justice and Police
findings.builder: Huawei; Radio, Film & TV Design and Research Institute (DRFT)
findings.financier: Government of China via Ministry of Commerce (EUR 10m grant Phase 1; USD 5m Phase 2)
findings.summary: China-funded Safe City (Road Monitoring) project: Huawei-contracted Phase 1 put about 300 CCTV cameras in Paramaribo with a DNVS command centre (Dec 2018); Phase 2 added cameras in Wanica and other districts, 378 cameras by 2022.

sources.publisher: AidData (William & Mary) Chinese development finance dataset

findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc on AidData naming Huawei as contractor; Key News confirms the Chinese-aid project and earlier phases but names no vendor, so corroboration of the controller is not met. Grants not converted (EUR 10m). Planned licence-plate and sound recording per AidData. A rights group lawsuit challenges its legal basis; not a reversal.

findings.controller: Not stated in Phase 3 reporting (AidData lists Huawei as contractor for all phases)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Justice and Police; Korps Politie Suriname
findings.builder: China Railway Construction Electrification Bureau Group
findings.financier: Government of China (USD 15m grant, China-aid fund)
findings.summary: Safe City 3, a USD 15m Chinese grant signed January 2023, broke ground January 2025 for about 650 cameras at 100 sites; by February 2026 police said cameras with licence-plate recognition were active across most districts.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: no Phase 3 source names the camera or platform vendor; the named builder is a Chinese civil contractor, which does not set the pole. Likely prc if Huawei continued from Phases 1-2, which a reviewer should check. Tier 5 on police statement of nationwide active cameras. All opened sources S3, none S1/S2, so not corroborated.

findings.controller: EllaLink (Caribbean Gateway cable system owner); equipment vendor not stated
findings.summary: State operator Telesur signed a letter of intent to connect Suriname to EllaLink's planned Caribbean Gateway subsea cable, linking to Europe via EllaLink's transatlantic system with onward links to Brazil and the US.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null because the cable rule keys on the equipment vendor, which is not stated; EllaLink is a European-based operator, so third is plausible. Tier 1 letter of intent only. Both reports appeared the same day and likely derive from one release; reviewer may discount corroboration.

facilities.null_reason: one search found only Telesur's commercial Datasur hosting service; no data-centre or AI-campus project since 2023 surfaced

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases, deployments or licence decisions surfaced in facilities, models or network searches; no dedicated search

models.null_reason: one search for government AI partnerships with frontier providers returned nothing on Suriname

research_gaps: Vendor of Safe City 3 cameras and command-centre platform (Huawei, Hikvision, Dahua?) and who operates it; Ministry of Justice and Police or government (CBB/NII) releases not checked.
Current RAN/core vendor for Telesur 4G/5G and for Digicel Suriname (Ericsson supplied Digicel sites in 2008; not reconfirmed).
Status of the Huawei-built National Broadband Network loan restructuring with China Exim (arrears about USD 107m in 2023) and any effect on Huawei's role.
Outcome of the Foundation December 8, 1982 lawsuit challenging the legal basis of Safe City surveillance.
Supplier of the EllaLink Caribbean Gateway and of the Suriname-Guyana Submarine Cable System; any HMN Tech involvement not checked.
Telesur's announced partnership with Liberty Networks (seen in search results, not opened).
